To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) the glycaemic response is not always correlated with the insulin response, and 2) there was no correlation between the metabolic response and family history of DM, duration of DM, BMI and FPG.

the glycaemic response to a mixed meal is greater than that to a high protein meal and that the insulinogenic response to a high fat meal is greater than or equal to that to a high fat or high protein meal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of a high protein diet on the metabolic responses of non-insulin-dependent diabetics (NIDDM) to meals with different compositions.
the study of the postprandial glucose response to meals with different compositions in non-insulinependent diabetes.
the effects of a high-protein diet in the treatment of diabetes mellitus.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the heterogeneity of the glycaemic response to the different nutrient compositions in NIDDM is not due to a difference in insulin secretion, but is due to the different glucose absorption from the intestine.
the postprandial glycometabolic responses in NIDDM are highly heterogeneous and the heterogeneity is not related to any of the clinical parameters examined in the present study.
NIDDM patients are a heterogeneous group with respect to the metabolic responses to different nutrient stimulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the postprandial responses of plasma glucose, insulin and pancreatic glucagon in NIDDM are heterogeneous and the heterogeneity cannot be classified into definite subtypes.

NIDDM has the nearly intact capacity in insulin secretion in response to a protein-rich or a fat-rich meal and the difficulty for subclassification according to the glyceamic and hormone responses to these meals.
the heterogeneity in NIDDM patients is not only in the degree of glucose intolerance, but also in the pattern of glucose and hormone responses to various kinds of meals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the best diet for people with diabetes should be individualized.
the best way to control your diabetes is by following the advice of your doctor and by taking care of your health.
we need to eat more protein and less carbohydrates to control our blood sugar and lose weight.
